Uses the creature survey; without creature data or faction templates nothing is surveyed and only the area floor counts. |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:CreatureSurveyRadius` | `int` | `100` | live | The radius in yards around each graveyard the creature survey counts hostile creature spawns in (0..300; 0 turns the survey off). The survey runs with the graveyard terrain lookup, off the world thread, when the atlas is built. |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:Enabled` | `bool` | `false` | live | Run the population manager (off by default). Off: no bot is created, started, parked or moved by it. |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:ExcludedZones` | `uint[]` | `[]` | live | Area table zone ids bots are never placed in (at most 256, no duplicates). Capitals and cities are never used. |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:Factions` | `PopulationFactions` | `Both` | live | The factions bots are created for (Both by default). Values: `Both`, `Alliance`, `Horde`. |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:FreshGraduateLevel` | `int` | `6` | live | The level at which a start home widens to FreshZoneHomeRadius (2..60). A leave-home quest (see LeaveHomeLevelMargin) is allowed only from here. |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:FreshLaunch` | `bool` | `false` | live | Fresh-launch mode (off by default; live): new bots the population creates stay level 1 with their default starting kit at their race's native start location (no boost, no teleport), the race and class mix stays balanced across both factions, and the level bands, the zone atlas and relocation are bypassed (the target is one pool; bots level up on their own). |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:FreshReleaseLevel` | `int` | `10` | live | The level at which a graduated home is replaced by the town homes of the progression (TownProgression; removed when that is off) (2..60; at least FreshGraduateLevel, equal skips the widened home). 10 puts the bot in the town of the next zone as it finishes its start zone. |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:FreshStartHome` | `bool` | `true` | live | Fresh launch: give each new bot its race's start area as a home (live, on by default). The home is a circle of FreshStartHomeRadius yards round the race's start position, clipped to the start zone, so a level 1 bot works the quests and creatures of its own valley and does not wander into the next zone's mobs or onto the Deeprun Tram. It graduates with the level: from FreshGraduateLevel the circle widens to FreshZoneHomeRadius (still clipped to the start zone), from FreshReleaseLevel the home becomes the town homes of TownProgression (with it off, the home is removed and the bot travels on by its own goals). Off: new bots get no home and no start-zone cap applies. The population's sweep also gives a running fresh-launch bot that has no home one for its level. |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:FreshStartHomeRadius` | `int` | `1100` | live | The radius in yards of the start home of a bot below FreshGraduateLevel (50..5000), zone-clipped. 1100 reaches the farthest turn-in of the class quests of the start areas (the dwarf priest's, 1078 yards from Coldridge Valley). Quests of everyone else are held to the start valley itself (400 to 540 yards, per area), which keeps the level 5 breadcrumbs to the next town for the graduated home. |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:FreshStartZoneCap` | `int` | `40` | live | The most bots one start area (Northshire, Coldridge Valley, Shadowglen, Valley of Trials, Camp Narache, Deathknell; the dwarf and gnome share one, as do the orc and troll) may hold under a start home (0..1000; 0 = no cap). A fresh-launch creation picks the least crowded area the chosen faction and class can start in; when every area is at the cap creation is deferred (the rush waits and says so) until bots graduate. |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:FreshZoneHomeRadius` | `int` | `4500` | live | The radius in yards of the graduated home, between FreshGraduateLevel and FreshReleaseLevel (50..5000). 4500 covers every starter zone end-to-end from its level-1 spawn while ZoneClipped keeps the bot inside its start zone. |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:IntervalSeconds` | `int` | `10` | live | Seconds of world time between two passes of the control loop (2..600). |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:LeaveHomeLevelMargin` | `int` | `0` | live | A quest whose turn-in NPC is outside a graduated home (a leave-home quest) needs the bot to be at least its QuestLevel minus this many levels (0..10), and never below its MinLevel. A bot under a start home takes none; a bot with no home is not affected. |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:MaxCreatePerMinute` | `int` | `4` | live | The most new bot characters created per minute of world time (0..600; 0 creates none and only restarts parked bots). |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:MaxParksPerInterval` | `int` | `2` | live | The most bots parked in one pass (1..500). |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:MaxRelocationsPerInterval` | `int` | `2` | live | The most bots relocated in one pass (0..50). |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:MaxStartsPerInterval` | `int` | `4` | live | The most bots started or created in one pass (1..500). |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:MinRunSeconds` | `int` | `300` | live | Anti-churn: a bot the population started is not parked for the tick budget until it has run this many seconds of world time (0..3600; 0 = no minimum). Over the target such a bot is still parked, last. |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:OutlevelMargin` | `int` | `2` | live | How many levels a bot may be above the highest level of its zone before it is relocated (0..10). |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:ParkWhenOverBudget` | `bool` | `true` | live | Park (stop) the least useful bots the population owns while the tick p95 is over the budget (on by default). Off: only stop adding. |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:Relocation` | `PopulationRelocation` | `Teleport` | live | What happens to a bot that out-levelled its zone or is below it (Teleport by default). Values: `Off`, `Teleport`. |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:ResumeBelowPct` | `int` | `80` | live | Adding bots resumes only while the tick p95 is below this percentage of TickP95BudgetMs (10..99). Between it and the budget the population holds, which keeps it from adding and parking in turns. |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:RushBrakeP95Ms` | `int` | `0` | live | The safety brake of `.playerbot population rush`: the rush pauses while the world tick p95 is above this many milliseconds in RushBrakeWindows consecutive windows of RushBrakeWindowSeconds seconds (50..10000). 0 (the default) means 1.5 times TickP95BudgetMs, so the brake follows the budget the population itself keeps. |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:RushBrakeWindowSeconds` | `int` | `5` | live | The length of one brake window in real seconds (1..60). The default 5 s with 3 windows pauses a rush after about 15 s over the ceiling. |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:RushBrakeWindows` | `int` | `3` | live | The consecutive windows over the RushBrakeP95Ms ceiling that pause a rush, and under the resume line that lift the pause (1..20). |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:SecondaryStayMaxMinutes` | `int` | `90` | live | The longest time in minutes (5..1440; at least SecondaryStayMinMinutes) a bot stays at its level-band town. |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:SecondaryStayMinMinutes` | `int` | `30` | live | The shortest time in minutes (5..1440) a bot stays at its level-band town before it heads to the capital. Each bot's stay is fixed per bot (by its id) between this and SecondaryStayMaxMinutes, so a fleet does not move in step. |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:SpawnsPerBot` | `int` | `3` | live | Zone capacity: a zone takes no new or relocated bot once its assigned bots reach the zone's level-fitting outdoor creature spawns (on the surface, not indoors or underground, hostile to the bot's faction) divided by this many (0..100; 0 turns the cap off). Keeps a small zone such as Deadwind Pass (47 surface spawns, 600 s respawn) from taking a hundred bots that find every creature dead. The spawn survey runs off the world thread; until it is in, no zone is capped. |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:TargetOnline` | `int` | `0` | live | The number of managed bots to keep running (0..5000). The effective target is the lower of this and `World:Playerbots:MaxBots`. Bots an operator created count towards it but are never stopped by the population: the running ones are taken off the top, and what is left (the population's own share) is what the bands split by weight. An operator's bot never counts in a band, so a band full of operator bots still gets its share of population bots. Above the target only the bots the population owns are parked. 0 parks every bot the population owns. |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:TickP95BudgetMs` | `int` | `60` | live | The world tick time budget in milliseconds (5..1000): the 95th percentile of the tick body duration over the last WindowTicks ticks. Above it the population stops adding bots and, with ParkWhenOverBudget, parks some. |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:TownBandMargin` | `int` | `0` | live | Levels a bot stays at its level-band town past the maximum level of the town's band before the next town takes it (0..10; the hysteresis margin of the band change). 0: it moves when its level reaches the maximum. |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:TownCap` | `int` | `60` | live | The most bots one level-band town (secondary) may hold (0..1000; 0 = no cap). Bots spread over the towns of their band, least populated first; when every town of the band is at the cap the least populated still takes the bot. |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:TownCaps` | `string` | `""` | live | Per-town caps that replace TownCap, as a comma-separated list of key=cap (for example "sentinel-hill=30,thelsamar=80"; the keys are those of PopulationTownProgression.Rows, caps 0..1000, 0 = no cap). Empty: TownCap for every town. |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:TownHomeRadius` | `int` | `4500` | live | The radius in yards of a secondary town home (50..5000), zone-clipped. 4500 covers the whole zone so its quests stay allowed; an idle bot still lingers at the town centre. |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:TownProgression` | `bool` | `true` | live | Town progression (on by default; needs FreshLaunch and FreshStartHome): from FreshReleaseLevel a bot has two homes, its faction capital (the master) and the town of its level band (the secondary, `PopulationTownProgression`), and lives at one of them at a time: SecondaryStayMin/MaxMinutes at the secondary, CapitalStayMin/MaxMinutes at the capital, and again. The secondary follows the level (the next town once the level reaches the cap of the band); a town whose centre cannot be found in the world data is reported once and the bot falls back to the towns that did resolve (or, with none, no home); a bot with no secondary that fits keeps no town home at all, so it explores instead of waiting at a capital. Off: a bot past FreshReleaseLevel has no home. |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:TownProgressionTeleport` | `bool` | `true` | live | The teleport of a town home (on by default): a bot whose new town lies on another continent, across the water of Teldrassil or farther than TownWalkYards takes the one return teleport (the Home teleport rules and cooldown) when it is homed there. Off: bots reach a town by their own means only (on foot, by taxi, and, with World:Playerbots:Travel on and a return mode other than Walk, by boat, zeppelin or mage portal: docs/areas/playbots.md, Travel); a town they cannot reach so is not assigned to that bot (it takes a town it can walk to; with none it keeps a home that is not a town home, or has none, and explores) and one Info anomaly per reason says so. The progression's own moves (the town cycle, a new band town, the Danger rule on the way to a town) then never teleport. The Home options' returns of a displaced bot still do, as for any home: from another map (OtherMap), a walk set aside as blocked (WalkBlocked), the Teleport return mode, an unsafe spirit-healer landing, and stalled ground. A bot on Teldrassil, whose only way off is a boat, therefore has no town secondary unless it may take the boat (or this option is on). |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:TownWalkYards` | `int` | `4500` | live | The longest trip in yards (100..20000) a bot with a town home walks to it on the same continent; farther, or across the water of Teldrassil, or to another continent, it takes the one return teleport (the Home teleport rules and cooldown). 4500 yards is about 11 minutes on foot. With World:Playerbots:Travel on (and a return mode other than Walk), a home across the sea is travelled to by boat, zeppelin or portal first, and the teleport is the fallback when no journey can begin. |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:TramMinLevel` | `int` | `10` | live | A bot below this level that has no home takes no Deeprun Tram or lift trip (0..60; 0 = no limit). The live fresh launch sent about 76 level 1 bots to Stormwind quests by the tram. |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:WindowTicks` | `int` | `200` | live | The ticks measured after every start, creation, park or relocation before the next decision (20..4096). A pass that finds fewer fresh ticks holds, so a decision never reacts to ticks from before the last change. |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:ZoneLevelSlack` | `int` | `4` | live | How many levels below a placement's floor a bot may be while the floor is at most ZoneLevelSlackMaxFloor (0..10). The floor is the level of the sub-area the graveyard stands in, or the zone's lowest sub-area level when the terrain does not know; a starter zone's is level 4 to 7, so the default 4 lets a level 1 bot start there. Above ZoneLevelSlackMaxFloor the slack shrinks by one level for every two floor levels, to 0. A bot below every place of its zone it could have been put is relocated like an out-levelled one. |
| `World:Playerbots:Population:ZoneLevelSlackMaxFloor` | `int` | `12` | live | The highest placement floor that gets the whole ZoneLevelSlack (1..60). Above it the slack shrinks by one level for every two floor levels (default: 3 at floors 13-14, 2 at 15-16, 1 at 17-18, 0 from 19), so a level 38 bot is not placed at a level 41 graveyard. 60 gives every floor the whole slack (the rule before the taper). |
| `World:Playerbots:RestoreOnStartup` | `bool` | `false` | - | Log the saved managed bots back in when the world starts. |
| `World:Playerbots:Risk:DangerMemorySeconds` | `int` | `300` | live | Seconds a bot remembers the creatures it retreated from or died to and the places that happened (0..86400): it does not pull a remembered creature again, and a remembered place raises the risk of fights there. |
| `World:Playerbots:Risk:DeathLoopMemorySeconds` | `int` | `2700` | live | Seconds a reported death-loop zone is avoided (0..86400). The 2700-second default outlives the 600-second loop window by 4.5 times, giving the bot time to finish a different errand before reconsidering the place. A second loop there doubles this duration, capped at one day. |
| `World:Playerbots:Risk:Enabled` | `bool` | `true` | live | Weigh fights and retreat from lost ones (on by default). Off: the bot takes the nearest target and fights to the end. |
| `World:Playerbots:Risk:NearlyWonHealthPct` | `float` | `20` | live | A fight against a single enemy at or below this health percentage is nearly won and is not abandoned (0..60), unless the bot would die in less than half the time it needs to finish it. |
| `World:Playerbots:Risk:PartyRetreatOnWipe` | `bool` | `true` | live | A bot in a real player's group follows its master's lead and never retreats on its own judgement; with this on (default) it does retreat when the group is wiping (the master dead, or half the group or more). |
| `World:Playerbots:Risk:RecoverHealthPct` | `float` | `80` | live | After a retreat (or before a pull it is too hurt for) the bot recovers to this health and mana percentage (10..100). |
| `World:Playerbots:Risk:RestManaBelowPct` | `float` | `35` | live | A bot that spends mana and has less than this percentage left (0..100; 0 turns it off) recovers before its next pull when the fight would be fine at full health and mana, instead of pulling with nothing to cast. |
| `World:Playerbots:Risk:RetreatHealthPct` | `float` | `35` | live | A losing bot retreats once its health falls to this percentage (5..95); one about to die retreats at any health. |
| `World:Playerbots:Risk:Tolerance` | `float` | `1` | live | The aggressiveness knob (0.25..4, 1 by default). It scales the risk a bot accepts for a given reward before a pull and how far behind it may fall in a fight before it retreats: 2 takes fights twice as dangerous, 0.5 only half. |
| `World:Playerbots:Scenarios:Enabled` | `bool` | `false` | - | Let an Administrator run registered bot scenarios against the live world (off by default). |
| `World:Playerbots:Scenarios:MaxDurationSeconds` | `int` | `120` | - | Wall-clock bound of one scenario run in seconds (5..600). |
| `World:Playerbots:Scenarios:StepTimeoutSeconds` | `int` | `20` | - | Default bound of one WaitUntil step in seconds (1..300). |
| `World:Playerbots:SlowThinkLogMs` | `double` | `50` | live | A single bot think longer than this many milliseconds is logged with its bot, goal, phases and path searches (`PlayerbotSlowThinkLog`; 0 = off, 0..60000). A think over it only because of garbage-collector pauses (think time minus GC pause under the threshold) is counted as `bot-brain/think-gc-stall` at Info instead of `think-slow`. Live: `.reload config` applies a change at once. |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Emotes:Enabled` | `bool` | `true` | live | Let an idle bot wave at (CMSG_TEXT_EMOTE) or greet with /say a real player of its faction standing within 8 yards, at most once per bot and player in 30 minutes, once per player in 10 minutes, once per bot in 5 minutes and twelve times a minute in all (on by default). A player who ignores the bot is never greeted. |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Events:Enabled` | `bool` | `true` | live | Let bots take part in the world's events (on by default). Off: festival places are given up (the bots go back to the inn at their next idle think) and no event line or emote is made. |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Events:Holidays:CelebrateChance` | `int` | `60` | live | The percent chance (0..100, default 60) that a bot celebrates a festival on a given day; rolled per bot per festival per day (the day changes for each bot at a time of its own). Sociable bots celebrate more often: `p = 1 - (1 - c)^(0.5 + sociability)`, which is exactly `c` at sociability 0.5. 0 sends nobody, 100 every bot. |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Events:Holidays:EmoteMaxSeconds` | `int` | `90` | live | The longest gap between two celebration emotes of one bot, in seconds (5..3600, not below `EmoteMinSeconds`, default 90). |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Events:Holidays:EmoteMinSeconds` | `int` | `30` | live | The shortest gap between two celebration emotes of one bot, in seconds (5..3600, default 30). |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Events:Holidays:EmotesPerAnchorMinute` | `int` | `3` | live | The festival text emotes around one anchor per minute, players in range or not (0..30, default 3). |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Events:Holidays:EmotesPerListenerMinute` | `int` | `2` | live | The festival text emotes one real player receives per minute from all bots together (0..10, default 2; 0 sends none while a player is in range). |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Events:Holidays:Enabled` | `bool` | `true` | live | Gather and celebrate at running festivals (on by default; `Social:Events:Enabled` is the master switch). |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Events:Holidays:ExcludedEvents` | `string` | `""` | live | Game event ids that are never treated as a festival or part of one, separated by commas and/or spaces (`"12, 24 25"`; each 1..65535, at most 64; empty: none). A string so that a reload compares it by value. |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Events:Holidays:MaxPerGossipAnchor` | `int` | `6` | live | The most bots around one festival NPC that only talks (1..20, default 6). |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Events:Holidays:MaxPerServiceAnchor` | `int` | `3` | live | The most bots around one festival quest giver or vendor (0..10, default 3; 0 keeps bots away from them). |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Events:Holidays:MaxPerTown` | `int` | `24` | live | The most bots celebrating in one town per team (1..200, default 24). |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Events:Holidays:SpotBackoffMinutes` | `int` | `30` | live | The minutes a festival NPC whose spot a bot could not reach is set aside for that bot, and a town whose crowd was attacked by a player is set aside for that team (1..1440, default 30). |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Events:Holidays:SpotRadiusYards` | `int` | `250` | live | How far from the town centre a festival NPC may stand to count, in yards (20..1000, default 250); it must also be inside the bot's home. |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Events:Holidays:TalkBotGapMinutes` | `int` | `20` | live | The minutes between two festival lines of the same bot (1..1440, default 20). |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Events:Holidays:TalkEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | live | Let bots say the arrival line and the named event remark (on by default; chat must be on as well). |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Events:Holidays:TalkZoneGapSeconds` | `int` | `120` | live | The seconds between two festival lines in the same zone, whichever bot (1..86400, default 120). |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Gratitude:Enabled` | `bool` | `true` | live | Let bots thank whoever helped them (on by default). Off: no emote, no line, no favour. |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Gratitude:MaxTipCopper` | `int` | `10000` | live | The most copper a tip may be for a level 60 bot (a lower level tips proportionally less; never more than 1% of the bot's gold). 0 turns tips off (default 10000, one gold). |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Gratitude:TipChance` | `float` | `0.05` | live | The chance (0..1), before the bot's Generosity trait scales it, that a thanks to a well-liked human helper is a gold tip by trade (default 0.05). |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:GuildChat:Enabled` | `bool` | `true` | live | Let bots say a short line in guild chat (on by default): a welcome, congratulations on a level, a note on a boss or a battleground won, and some small talk. The lines go through the bot chat service (`World:Playerbots:Chat`: its providers, spend caps and safety screening), so nothing is said while `Chat:Enabled` is off; and only while a real player who can read guild chat is online. |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:GuildChat:MessagesPerHour` | `int` | `4` | live | The most lines the bots of one guild say per hour (0..60; 0 keeps them silent). |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Guilds:AffinityInvites` | `bool` | `true` | live | Let a guild's master or officer invite a guildless, same-team character it knows and likes (`GuildInviteAffinity`, `GuildInviteMinFamiliarity`; at most one invitation per character per `GuildInviteCooldownDays`), and let a guildless bot accept the invitation of a character it likes (`GuildAcceptAffinity`) (on by default). |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Guilds:Creation` | `PlayerbotGuildCreation` | `Auto` | live | How a guild is founded (`PlayerbotGuildCreation.Auto` by default). Values: `Auto`, `Charter`, `ClientCreate`. |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Guilds:Enabled` | `bool` | `true` | live | Let bots found guilds and invite other bots (on by default). Off: no new guild forms and no bot is invited; a bot still answers the invitations it receives (by `InvitePolicy`) and the guilds that exist go on. |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Guilds:GuildAcceptAffinity` | `int` | `30` | live | The affinity toward the inviter at which a guildless bot accepts a guild invitation; it declines below it (-100..100). |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Guilds:GuildInviteAffinity` | `int` | `60` | live | The affinity an officer needs toward a guildless character before it invites it (-100..100). |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Guilds:GuildInviteCooldownDays` | `int` | `7` | live | Days before the same character is invited again (0..365). |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Guilds:GuildInviteMinFamiliarity` | `int` | `8` | live | The familiarity an officer needs with a guildless character before it invites it (0..1000). |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Guilds:InvitePolicy` | `PlayerbotInvitePolicy` | `GuildOrFriends` | live | Who may invite a bot into a guild, and whose charter a bot signs (`PlayerbotInvitePolicy.GuildOrFriends` by default): the same rules as `World:Playerbots:Party:InvitePolicy`, and the names in `World:Playerbots:Party:Allowlist` are always accepted. Another bot's invitation into a guild the founding bots are building is always accepted. Values: `None`, `GuildOrFriends`, `Anyone`, `Affinity`. |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Guilds:MaxBotGuilds` | `int` | `4` | live | The most guilds led by a registered bot at once (0..64; 0 founds none). Lowering it disbands nothing: it only stops new foundings. |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Guilds:TargetSize` | `int` | `25` | live | The most members of a bot guild, pending invitations counted (2..500). |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Helping:AnswerHelp` | `bool` | `true` | live | Let a bot that is asked for help (a targeted help emote, or a help yell or say from someone close) decide whether to answer it (on by default). |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Helping:BuffCooldownMinutes` | `int` | `30` | live | The least minutes between two buffs a bot gives the same stranger (0..1440). |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Helping:BuffStrangers` | `bool` | `true` | live | Let a bot occasionally cast one of its class buffs (the ones it casts on groupmates) on a same-faction stranger (on by default). |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Helping:Enabled` | `bool` | `true` | live | Let bots look for strangers in trouble and help them (on by default). Off: no scan, and no call for help is answered either. |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Helping:MaxAnswersPerCall` | `int` | `2` | live | The most bots that answer one call for help (1..16, 2 by default): a call is heard by every free bot in earshot, but a crowd is not what the asker needs. |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Helping:ResurrectMaxCorpseMinutes` | `int` | `10` | live | The longest (minutes) a body may have lain dead for a stranger's resurrection to be offered (1..60, 10 by default), counted from the death when the server knows it, else from the scan's first sight of it. |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Helping:ResurrectStrangers` | `bool` | `true` | live | Let a bot whose class can resurrect resurrect a dead same-faction stranger with a recent corpse, once per corpse (on by default). |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Helping:TroubleRadiusYards` | `float` | `30` | live | How far (yards) from an idle bot a unit in trouble may be and still be noticed (1..100). |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Initiative:CommentBotGapMinutes` | `int` | `10` | live | The minutes between two comments of the same bot (1..1440, default 10). |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Initiative:CommentZoneGapSeconds` | `int` | `60` | live | The seconds between two comments in the same zone, whichever bot (1..86400, default 60). |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Initiative:CommentsEnabled` | `bool` | `true` | live | Let bots comment on their surroundings (on by default). |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Initiative:Enabled` | `bool` | `true` | live | Let bots open conversations and comment on their surroundings (on by default). |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Initiative:MaxOpeningsPerPass` | `int` | `4` | live | The most openings (all bots together) in one pass of the social feature (1..64, default 4). |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Initiative:OpeningCooldownMinutes` | `int` | `30` | live | The minutes before any bot opens with the same real player again (1..1440, default 30); an opening they ignored doubles it each time. |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Lists:ChangeSpacingSeconds` | `int` | `60` | live | The least seconds between two list changes of one bot (1..3600). |
| `World:Playerbots:Social:Lists:Enabled` | `bool` | `true` | live | Let bots manage their friend and ignore lists by affinity (on by default). |

| `World:Playerbots:SyncPathQueryMaxMs` | `int` | `0` | live | The longest wall time in milliseconds one navigation-mesh search may take on the world thread (0 = no bound, else 10..60000): a search past it stops as one that ran out of nodes does (capped). Live 2026-10-24: one bot think spent 2 168 ms in a single 32 768-node search. Live: `.reload config`. |
| `World:Playerbots:Taxi:BackoffMinutes` | `int` | `10` | live | The longest, in minutes, a flight node is backed off after trips from it failed (the server refused the flight, the flight master could not be reached, or none stood where the node is): the per-node cap on the schedule of `World:Playerbots:Travel` (`TransitBackoffSeconds` doubling to `TransitBackoffMaxSeconds`). Only the failing node waits; the bot walks, or flies from another known node, meanwhile (1..1440; default 10). |

| `World:Playerbots:Taxi:MinRouteYards` | `float` | `600` | live | A trip is flown only when the straight line from the bot to where it is going is at least this many yards (100..20000; default 600). Shorter trips are walked. |
| `World:Playerbots:ThinkBudgetMaxMs` | `double` | `30` | - | The most wall time (ms, at least `ThinkBudgetMinMs`, at most 200) a world tick spends on the bots' thinks, however idle the rest of the tick is. |
| `World:Playerbots:ThinkBudgetMinMs` | `double` | `8` | - | The least wall time (ms, 1..200) a world tick spends on the bots' thinks, however loaded the tick is: the guarantee that a busy server still thinks (`PlayerbotThinkBudget`). At least one bot always thinks per tick. Equal to `ThinkBudgetMaxMs` it is a fixed budget. Raised, up to `ThinkBudgetMaxMs`, to what walking every bot within `ThinkStarvedGapMs` takes at the measured cost of a think (`PlayerbotThinkBudget.CoverageMs`): 8 ms covers about 400 bots (1.3 ms a visit, 50 ms ticks, 3 ms of fights) and 1000 bots need about 16 ms, up to the ceiling: the bots then take more of each tick. The walk is sized from the configured tick interval, not the real one: a real tick longer than the configured one does not raise the budget (that would slow the ticks further), so a full pass of the bots then takes longer than the bound it was sized for (1000 bots at about 10 bots a tick: 8 to 30 s at 80 to 260 ms ticks). The motion lease and the think-starved report follow the measured pass instead (`ThinkStarvedGapMs`). |
| `World:Playerbots:ThinkBudgetTickShare` | `double` | `0.6` | - | The share (0.05..0.95) of a tick's slack (tick interval minus the time the world spent on everything but the bots) the bots' work may take; the think budget is this share of the slack less what the bots already used this tick, between the min and the max. |
| `World:Playerbots:ThinkIntervalMs` | `int` | `500` | - | Milliseconds between two decisions of a bot (50..60000). |
| `World:Playerbots:ThinkStarvedGapMs` | `int` | `10000` | - | A bot that goes longer than this many milliseconds (1000..3600000) of world time without a think is reported once per episode as a "cadence think-starved" anomaly (`PlayerbotAnomalies`); 0 turns the report off. The default is the ghost walk's stuck bound (`PlayerbotRecovery.StuckMs`). The report fires only for a bot that falls behind the rotation: its bound is the larger of this value and 1.5 times the measured time of a full pass of the main think lane (three times this value until a pass is measured), so a rotation that is slow for every bot alike raises nothing. The think budget is still sized from this value unraised. |

| `World:Playerbots:Travel:Enabled` | `bool` | `true` | live | Let bots plan multi-leg trips to far places (on by default). Off: no trip is planned and a far goal stays where its caller leaves it. |

| `World:Playerbots:Travel:MageServiceRadiusYards` | `float` | `150` | live | A bot asks for a portal only from a mage within this many yards of it, on its map (10..1000; default 150). |
| `World:Playerbots:Travel:MaxTravelSpendCopper` | `uint` | `10000` | live | The most copper one trip may spend on fares, fees and reagents together (0..10000000; default 10000, one gold). 0: only free means (walking, boats, zeppelins, the tram, lifts, the hearthstone, a free portal, the bot's own teleport when it has the rune). |
| `World:Playerbots:Travel:TransitBackoffMaxSeconds` | `int` | `300` | live | The longest wait (seconds) before a failed transit point is tried again (10..86400; default 300). Must not be below `TransitBackoffSeconds`. |
| `World:Playerbots:Travel:TransitBackoffSeconds` | `int` | `60` | live | The first wait (seconds) before a bot tries a transit point again (one flight master's node, tram platform, lift, dock) that just failed it; each further failure of the same point doubles the wait up to `TransitBackoffMaxSeconds` (10..3600; default 60). |
| `World:Playerbots:Travel:Zeppelins` | `bool` | `true` | live | Let Horde bots ride the zeppelins (Orgrimmar - Undercity, Orgrimmar - Grom'gol, Undercity - Grom'gol; on by default). |

## `World:Playerbots:Qa`

| Key | Type | Default | Reload | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `World:Playerbots:Qa:AutoPruneHours` | `int` | `0` | - | Hours after which a finding not seen again is forgotten on every pass, counted from the later of its last sighting and the server start (so a restart prunes nothing at once). A finding that holds a GitHub issue is never forgotten, and GitHub is never touched. 0 (default) is off; the same as `.playerbot qa prune #hours` (0..8760). |
| `World:Playerbots:Qa:Directory` | `string` | `"qa"` | - | The folder of the findings file, the exports (`report.md`, `report.json`) and the dry-run issues (`pending-issues/`): relative to the profile folder, or absolute. |
| `World:Playerbots:Qa:Enabled` | `bool` | `true` | - | Aggregate the bot stall, death-loop, fault and missing-data warnings into findings (on by default; it is cheap and never touches the world thread). |
| `World:Playerbots:Qa:ExportIntervalSeconds` | `int` | `300` | - | Seconds between two passes that save the findings, write the exports and publish (10..86400). |
| `World:Playerbots:Qa:GitHub:AutoCloseMinQuietHours` | `int` | `72` | - | The least quiet time, in hours, before `AutoCloseQuietMultiple` may close an issue (1..8760, default 72), whatever the finding's usual gap. |
| `World:Playerbots:Qa:GitHub:AutoCloseQuietMultiple` | `int` | `0` | - | Close an open issue as completed when its finding has stopped: it was last seen on an older build, the running build is newer and has not met it, and it has been quiet (since the later of its last sighting and the reporter's start) for this many times its usual gap between occurrences ((last seen - first seen) / (count - 1)) and at least `AutoCloseMinQuietHours`. One comment says why; a recurrence on any later build counts as a regression of the build it was last seen on and reopens it (`ReopenOnRegression`). 0 (default) is off (0..1000). Quiet is not proof: a finding the bots simply stopped visiting looks the same. |
| `World:Playerbots:Qa:GitHub:CloseAbsorbedDuplicates` | `bool` | `false` | - | When findings are merged into one (the same problem met in several places) and each had its own issue, comment on the absorbed issue with a link to the surviving one and close it as not planned (a duplicate). Off (the default, so the first start after an upgrade can be checked: the start-up log lists every issue it would close, each with the surviving issue) keeps the absorbed issue open and untouched; the merge is recorded in the store either way. |
| `World:Playerbots:Qa:GitHub:CommentIntervalHours` | `int` | `24` | - | At most one comment per finding in this many hours (1..720). |
| `World:Playerbots:Qa:GitHub:Enabled` | `bool` | `false` | - | Report findings to GitHub (off by default). Enabled without `Publish` is a dry run: no network call is made. |
| `World:Playerbots:Qa:GitHub:GhPassToken` | `bool` | `false` | - | For `GhCli` only: hand the token from `TokenEnvironmentVariable` to `gh` as `GH_TOKEN` (off by default: `GITHUB_TOKEN` and `GH_TOKEN` are removed from the child so `gh` uses its own login). |
| `World:Playerbots:Qa:GitHub:GhPath` | `string` | `"gh"` | - | The `gh` executable for `Transport` = `GhCli`: a file name looked up on PATH (`gh`) or a full path (1..260 characters). |
| `World:Playerbots:Qa:GitHub:KindLabels` | `bool` | `false` | - | Add a per-kind label (`bot-qa:spell-unsupported`, `bot-qa:death-loop`, ...) to created issues besides `Labels` (off by default: the `gh` transport refuses a label that does not exist yet, so create the labels in the repository first). |
| `World:Playerbots:Qa:GitHub:Labels` | `string[]` | `["bot-qa"]` | - | The labels put on created issues; the first one is also how existing issues are listed (1..10 labels; a configured list replaces the default). |
| `World:Playerbots:Qa:GitHub:MaxCommentsPerHour` | `int` | `10` | - | The most comments added per rolling hour (0..1000; 0 adds none). |
| `World:Playerbots:Qa:GitHub:MaxIssuesPerHour` | `int` | `5` | - | The most issues created per rolling hour (0..1000; 0 creates none); the rest stay pending. |
| `World:Playerbots:Qa:GitHub:MaxListPages` | `int` | `10` | - | The most 100-issue pages read when looking for an existing issue (1..100). |
| `World:Playerbots:Qa:GitHub:MaxSpellIssuesPerDay` | `int` | `10` | - | The most spell issues created per rolling 24 hours (0..1000; 0 creates none), saved with the hourly caps. |
| `World:Playerbots:Qa:GitHub:MaxSpellIssuesPerPass` | `int` | `2` | - | The most spell issues (spell unsupported, refused, no effect) created in one publish pass (0..100; 0 creates none). Spell findings can be numerous on a first run; the hourly `MaxIssuesPerHour` still applies on top. |
| `World:Playerbots:Qa:GitHub:MaxStatusEditsPerHour` | `int` | `30` | - | The most live-status body edits per rolling hour (0..1000; 0 makes none), saved with the hourly caps. |
| `World:Playerbots:Qa:GitHub:MinDistinctBots` | `int` | `2` | - | A finding caused by bots is reported once this many different bots met it (1..10000); data findings of creature scripts are exempt. |
| `World:Playerbots:Qa:GitHub:MinOccurrences` | `int` | `3` | - | A finding is reported once it was seen this many times (1..1000000). |
| `World:Playerbots:Qa:GitHub:Publish` | `bool` | `false` | - | Really create issues and comments (off by default = dry run: the would-be issues are written to `qa/pending-issues/` and logged, nothing is sent). |
| `World:Playerbots:Qa:GitHub:ReopenClosed` | `bool` | `false` | - | Reopen a finding's issue when it was closed and the finding keeps happening (off by default: a closed issue is recorded as known and left alone). |
| `World:Playerbots:Qa:GitHub:ReopenOnRegression` | `bool` | `true` | - | Reopen a closed issue, with one comment (the new build, the occurrences on it, the distinct bots and a sample), when its finding recurs on a build other than the one it was observed closed on (a regression; a recurrence on the same build is a person's won't-fix and is left alone). Acts only while publishing is on, under the comment cap; never closes anything. |
| `World:Playerbots:Qa:GitHub:Repository` | `string` | `""` | - | The repository, `owner/repo` (required while enabled). |
| `World:Playerbots:Qa:GitHub:RequestTimeoutSeconds` | `int` | `15` | - | Seconds one GitHub request may take (1..120). |
| `World:Playerbots:Qa:GitHub:StatusUpdateMinutes` | `int` | `60` | - | Keep a live status block at the top of each open issue's body (last seen UTC, occurrences in all and on the running build, distinct bots), rewritten when the finding was seen again at least this many minutes after the time the block shows (0..10080; 0 is off). Comments come at most every `CommentIntervalHours`, so without it GitHub's view of when a finding last happened lags by up to a day; with it the lag is at most this long. A body edit sends no notification; edits are capped by `MaxStatusEditsPerHour`. |
| `World:Playerbots:Qa:GitHub:TokenEnvironmentVariable` | `string` | `"ARCANECORE_GITHUB_TOKEN"` | - | The name of the environment variable that holds a fine-grained token with Issues read and write on the repository (the value is never read from configuration and never logged). |
| `World:Playerbots:Qa:GitHub:Transport` | `PlayerbotQaGitHubTransport` | `Rest` | - | How issues are read and written: `Rest` (default; the GitHub REST API with the token from `TokenEnvironmentVariable`) or `GhCli` (runs the `gh` tool with an argument list and no shell, using the login of the user the server runs as; the token variable is not needed). Values: `Rest`, `GhCli`. |
| `World:Playerbots:Qa:MaxFindings` | `int` | `2000` | - | The most findings kept (10..100000); beyond it an unpublished finding is dropped, a one-off of a single bot first, then the lowest severity, then the oldest. A published or known-closed finding is never dropped. |
| `World:Playerbots:Qa:MaxSamples` | `int` | `5` | - | The newest evidence samples kept per finding (1..20). |
| `World:Playerbots:Qa:SignalQueueCapacity` | `int` | `4096` | - | Warnings waiting for the aggregator at once (64..1000000); a full queue drops the oldest and counts it. |
| `World:Playerbots:Qa:StaleHours` | `int` | `24` | - | Hours after which a finding not seen again and not published or known-closed is dropped, on load and on every pass (0..8760; 0 keeps them for ever). |
| `World:Playerbots:Qa:TickHangWarmupMinutes` | `int` | `5` | - | Minutes after the world starts ticking during which a tick hang is not reported to QA (start-up: cold grids, JIT, loading). 0 reports from the first tick (0..1440, default 5). |

## `World:RemoteAdmin`

| Key | Type | Default | Reload | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `World:RemoteAdmin:AgentLoginFile` | `string` | `"ra-token.txt"` | - | A file the daemon writes a fresh random token to at start; `@token &lt;token&gt;` logs in as the console (Administrator) without an account, for automation running as the same OS user (the file is readable by whoever can read the daemon's directory). Relative paths are under the daemon's base directory. Empty: token login off. |
| `World:RemoteAdmin:BindAddress` | `string` | `"127.0.0.1"` | - | The address to listen on. Default 127.0.0.1: only this machine can connect. Any other address exposes a clear-text protocol (passwords included) to the network; the daemon logs a warning when it is not a loopback address. |
| `World:RemoteAdmin:CommandTimeoutSeconds` | `int` | `1800` | - | Seconds a command that holds itself open (`.botctl wait`, `.botctl run`) may run before RA reports `#done error timeout` and reads the next line (the command itself goes on). |
| `World:RemoteAdmin:Enabled` | `bool` | `true` | - | Listen for RA connections. Default on (loopback only, see `BindAddress`). |
| `World:RemoteAdmin:FailedLoginDelayMs` | `int` | `1000` | - | The delay before answering a wrong login. |
| `World:RemoteAdmin:IdleTimeoutSeconds` | `int` | `3600` | - | Seconds a logged-in connection may stay silent (no command, no running command) before it is closed. 0: never. |
| `World:RemoteAdmin:LoginTimeoutSeconds` | `int` | `60` | - | Seconds a connection has to log in. |
| `World:RemoteAdmin:MaxConnections` | `int` | `8` | - | Concurrent connections; one more is refused with a message. |
| `World:RemoteAdmin:MaxFailedLogins` | `int` | `3` | - | Wrong logins a connection may make before it is closed (each one delayed by `FailedLoginDelayMs`). |
| `World:RemoteAdmin:MaxLineLength` | `int` | `16384` | - | The longest command line in bytes; a longer line closes the connection without running anything. |
| `World:RemoteAdmin:MinSecurity` | `AccountSecurity` | `Administrator` | - | The lowest account security that may log in (mangosd Ra.MinLevel, default Administrator). Values: `Player`, `Moderator`, `GameMaster`, `Administrator`. |
| `World:RemoteAdmin:Port` | `int` | `3443` | - | The TCP port (mangosd Ra.Port default 3443). |

## `World:Social`

| Key | Type | Default | Reload | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `World:Social:AllowTwoSideAddFriend` | `bool` | `false` | live | AllowTwoSide.AddFriend. |
| `World:Social:AllowTwoSideChannel` | `bool` | `false` | live | AllowTwoSide.Interaction.Channel. |
| `World:Social:AllowTwoSideGroup` | `bool` | `false` | live | AllowTwoSide.Interaction.Group. |
| `World:Social:AllowTwoSideGuild` | `bool` | `false` | live | AllowTwoSide.Interaction.Guild. |
| `World:Social:MaxChannelNameLength` | `int` | `255` | live | ArcaneCore hardening: the longest channel name (characters) a join accepts; a longer one gets INVALID_NAME and no channel is created. 0 = no cap. vmangos has none and the stock client's limit is UNVERIFIED (not captured from a real client). The default (255) assumes a chat edit box of that length, which is unconfirmed; if the client allows longer names, raise it or set 0. |
| `World:Social:MaxChannelPassphraseLength` | `int` | `255` | live | ArcaneCore hardening: the longest channel password (characters) accepted on join or when set; over it a join gets WRONG_PASSWORD and a set is ignored. 0 = no cap. Default 255, as for `MaxChannelNameLength`. |
| `World:Social:MaxJoinedChannels` | `int` | `0` | live | Most channels one player may be in; 0 = unlimited. vmangos has no cap (ChannelMgr.cpp:52-69), so the retail default is 0; a positive value is opt-in hardening (World:Social:MaxJoinedChannels). |
| `World:Social:OfflineLeaderDelaySeconds` | `int` | `300` | live | Seconds before an offline group leader yields to an online member. Zero disables the handoff. vmangos@0e3ff01 src/game/World.cpp:811,2063-2072 defaults to 300 seconds. |
| `World:Social:ReadyCheckAnswerIntervalMs` | `int` | `0` | live | ArcaneCore hardening: the shortest time (milliseconds) between two ready-check answers of one member that are forwarded to the leader; answers inside it are dropped (a dropped answer is not replayed, so the leader can keep a stale one), and a new ready check resets it. Off (0) by default, as in vmangos, which forwards every answer, pending check or not (GroupHandler.cpp HandleRaidReadyCheckOpcode): set it only to defend against a member spamming the leader. |
| `World:Social:VmangosChannelExtensions` | `bool` | `false` | live | The vmangos-only custom channel names: "World" becomes a General-flagged channel without join/leave announcements and "China" (or its Mandarin name) a Custom one without announcements (vmangos Channel.cpp:63-71). Retail 1.12 has neither, so they are ordinary custom channels unless this is on; it applies to channels created after the change. |

## Keys read by name

These keys are read directly rather than through an options class.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Crafting:Enabled` | `bool` | `true` | `false` leaves crafting (reagent check, tool check and the CREATE_ITEM effect) and profession-specialization gossip unregistered (read once by `CraftingFeature`); unset or unparsable keeps crafting enabled, the retail behaviour. |
| `Forms:ResetFistAttackTimeOnFormLoss` | `bool` | `false` | `true` gives a weapon-less hand the 2.0 s base attack time when a shapeshift form ends (read once by `FormStatFeature`); `false` keeps the retail 1.0 / 2.5 s of an unarmed hand. |
| `Items:CharStartOutfitDbcPath` | `string` | `null` | Build-5875 CharStartOutfit.dbc: a new character's starting items by race, class and gender, then the SQL starting items (read once by `ItemsFeature`). Unset keeps the SQL starting items only; a configured file that is unreadable or has another layout fails the item load (no silent fallback). |
| `Spells:RequireSpellFocus` | `bool` | `true` | `false` stops enforcing `SpellInfo.RequiresSpellFocus` on casts (read once by `SpellFocusFeature`); `true` is the retail behaviour. |
| `Startup:Strict` | `bool` | `false` | `true` makes a configuration warning fail start-up like an error (exit code 78); read by `ConfigReport.Run` in both daemons. |

## Aliases and framework sections

- `ChatRestrictionOptions`: `World:Chat:FloodMessageCount`, `World:Chat:FloodMessageDelaySeconds` and `World:Chat:FloodMuteSeconds` are bound twice: by `ChatFeature` into `ChatOptions` (documented in the `World:Chat` table) and by `ChatRestrictionFeature` into `ChatRestrictionOptions`, both with the same defaults. Set them once; both read them.
- `LootOptions.RewardRange`: `Loot:RewardRange` is computed from `Loot:GroupLootDistance`, `Loot:BossRewardDistanceBonus` and `Loot:RaidMapsUnlimitedRewardDistance`; it is not a key.
- `WorldRuntimeOptions.Perf`: `World:Perf:*` is an alias. `PerformanceLog` is the real section (`PerformanceLogOptions.SectionName`); `WorldServiceCollectionExtensions` copies it into `WorldRuntimeOptions.Perf` with a PostConfigure, so a `World:Perf:*` key is never read.
- `Logging` and `HostOptions` (`ShutdownTimeout`) belong to the .NET host, not to ArcaneCore; see the .NET documentation for their keys.
